section: Centre-State financial relations - Articles 264-293; taxes assigned, grants-in-aid, borrowing powers
subsections: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

Tax - levying, collecting and appropriating authority
Financial relations framework - Part, Articles, emergencies, Consolidated Fund

accepted.s: Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India with effect from which date?
o: 15 August 2017
1 July 2017
1 April 2016
1 April 2018
accepted.x: GST came into effect on 1 July 2017 pursuant to the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.
accepted.tq: Use the precise implementation date rather than the year of constitutional amendment.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the nature of GST in India?
o: Origin-based and applicable only to goods
Destination-based and applicable to goods and services
Origin-based and applicable only to services
Destination-based and applicable only to inter-State supplies
accepted.x: GST is a destination-based tax levied on the supply of goods and services.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the confusable terms origin-based and destination-based.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: The Goods and Services Tax subsumed approximately how many earlier taxes?
accepted.x: GST subsumed approximately 17 central and State indirect taxes.
accepted.tq: Test the approximate numerical figure directly with nearby alternatives.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: Which of the following sets consists of the principal components of GST mentioned in the Constitution and the GST framework?
o: CGST, SGST, IGST and UTGST
SGST, excise duty, IGST and service tax
CGST, customs duty, SGST and corporation tax
CGST, VAT, CST and UTGST
accepted.x: The GST structure comprises Central GST, State GST, Integrated GST and Union Territory GST.
accepted.tq: Use a complete-list question to distinguish GST components from subsumed taxes.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: A decision of the GST Council requires what proportion of the weighted votes?
o: Two-thirds of the weighted votes
Unanimous approval
A simple majority
Three-fourths of the weighted votes
accepted.x: A proposal in the GST Council requires at least three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting.
accepted.tq: Test the exact constitutional voting threshold against familiar majority figures.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: Why can neither the Union nor the States alone carry a decision in the GST Council?
o: Because the Union Finance Minister does not vote in the Council
Because the States have a veto over all GST matters
Because the Council requires unanimous approval in every matter
Because the Centre has one-third and the States together have two-thirds of the weighted votes, while three-fourths is required
accepted.x: The Centre has one-third and the States together have two-thirds of the weighted votes, whereas a decision requires three-fourths.
accepted.tq: Apply the voting weights and threshold instead of recalling either figure in isolation.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT presently included within the GST framework listed among the excluded sectors?
o: Natural gas
Alcohol for human consumption
Processed food products
Electricity
accepted.x: Crude oil, petrol, diesel, aviation turbine fuel, natural gas, electricity, alcohol for human consumption and real estate are listed outside GST. Processed food products are not included in that exclusion list.
accepted.tq: Find the item that does not belong to a closely related exclusion list.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: Under Article 246A, which legislative arrangement applies to GST?
o: Parliament and State Legislatures can both make GST laws, but only Parliament can legislate on inter-State supplies
Only Parliament can make laws on all GST matters
Parliament can legislate only on intra-State supplies
Only State Legislatures can make laws on GST within their territories
accepted.x: Article 246A gives concurrent GST legislative power to Parliament and State Legislatures, while Parliament alone legislates on inter-State supplies.
accepted.tq: Test the exception within a concurrent legislative power.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: The revenue from Integrated GST on inter-State supplies is intended to go to which State?
o: The State where the goods were manufactured
The destination State
The State where the supplier is registered
The State selected by the GST Council annually
accepted.x: Article 269A concerns IGST, with the revenue going to the destination State in accordance with the destination-based character of GST.
accepted.tq: Link the tax type with the destination-based principle and avoid the origin-state trap.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: Compensation Cess under the GST system was primarily imposed on which category of goods?
o: All exports
Land revenue and agricultural income
Essential agricultural inputs only
Luxury and sin goods
accepted.x: Compensation Cess on luxury and sin goods was used to fund compensation to States for GST-related revenue loss.
accepted.tq: Use the purpose-and-base combination rather than confusing cess with a general GST levy.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding GST compensation:
1. Compensation for revenue loss was promised by the 101st Constitutional Amendment.
2. The compensation arrangement ended after five years.
3. Cessation of GST compensation has been identified as a fiscal stress for Kerala.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the 101st Amendment promised compensation, the arrangement ended after five years, and its cessation has been cited as a fiscal stress for Kerala.
accepted.tq: Combine a constitutional promise, a time limit and a State-level fiscal consequence.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: In a situation where both Central and State GST authorities investigate the same entity, what direction was given by the Andhra Pradesh High Court in May 2026?
o: The authorities must decide among themselves which authority will proceed, without dual action
The investigation must be transferred to the GST Council
The State authority must always withdraw the investigation
Both authorities must proceed simultaneously
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh High Court held that the Central and State GST authorities must decide who proceeds, so that there is no dual action against the same entity.
accepted.tq: Test the practical consequence of overlapping authority through a short factual scenario.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: Which of the following is a criticism concerning State fiscal autonomy under the GST regime?
o: States obtained exclusive control over IGST
States acquired independent powers over all indirect taxes
States surrendered independent indirect-tax powers and concerns were raised about weighted voting
The Union surrendered its power to legislate on inter-State supplies
accepted.x: The GST framework has been criticised because States surrendered independent indirect-tax powers and because of concerns regarding the weighted voting structure.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise federalism concern instead of accepting an exaggerated transfer of powers.
accepted.sec: GST and state fiscal autonomy - compensation cess, GST Council voting weights

accepted.s: Cesses and surcharges levied by the Union are generally excluded from which pool?
o: The Public Account of India
The Consolidated Fund of India
The State Disaster Response Fund
The divisible pool under Article 270
accepted.x: Cesses and surcharges are excluded from the divisible pool under Article 270 and are therefore not ordinarily shared with States as part of that pool.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the divisible pool from the Consolidated Fund where Union revenues are received.
accepted.sec: Cesses and surcharges outside the divisible pool - trend and state concerns

accepted.s: Which of the following is cited as an example of the shift from basic duties towards cesses?
o: Land Revenue Cess imposed by every State
Agricultural Income Surcharge under Article 270
Municipal Service Cess under Article 266
Krishi Kalyan Cess
accepted.x: Krishi Kalyan Cess, Health and Education Cess, fuel cess and Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess are examples of the shift towards cesses.
accepted.tq: Select a named example from a cluster of related fiscal instruments.
accepted.sec: Cesses and surcharges outside the divisible pool - trend and state concerns

accepted.s: According to the cited 2025–26 estimate, approximately what proportion of gross tax revenue formed the divisible pool?
accepted.x: The divisible pool was estimated at approximately 81% of gross tax revenue in 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Separate the gross-tax-to-pool ratio from the State devolution percentage.
accepted.sec: Cesses and surcharges outside the divisible pool - trend and state concerns

accepted.s: The effective devolution to States was cited as approximately what percentage, compared with the 41% mandate?
accepted.x: The effective devolution was cited as approximately 30–32%, which is below the 41% mandate because cesses and surcharges are outside the divisible pool.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison between the effective figure and the mandated figure to avoid a reversed percentage.
accepted.sec: Cesses and surcharges outside the divisible pool - trend and state concerns

accepted.s: What was the principal feature of the 'grand bargain' proposed by the 16th Finance Commission in relation to cesses?
o: All cesses would be transferred directly to local bodies
States would accept a smaller share of a larger pool if most cesses were merged into regular taxes
States would receive a larger share of a smaller pool without any change in cesses
States would impose all Union cesses within their territories
accepted.x: The proposal envisaged States taking a smaller share of a larger pool if the Centre merged most cesses into regular taxes.
accepted.tq: Test both linked conditions of a policy proposal rather than only its title.
accepted.sec: Cesses and surcharges outside the divisible pool - trend and state concerns

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the 16th Finance Commission and cesses is correct?
o: It recommended a complete prohibition on all Union cesses
It made no recommendation to curb cesses and instead proposed a grand bargain
It transferred the power to levy cesses to State Legislatures
It included every surcharge automatically in the divisible pool
accepted.x: The 16th Finance Commission made no recommendation to curb cesses; its approach was to propose a grand bargain involving merger of most cesses into regular taxes.
accepted.tq: Use the NOT-recommended versus proposed-mechanism distinction.
accepted.sec: Cesses and surcharges outside the divisible pool - trend and state concerns

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes vertical and horizontal devolution?
o: Vertical devolution is between Union and States; horizontal devolution is among the States
Vertical devolution concerns taxes; horizontal devolution concerns borrowing alone
Vertical devolution is among States; horizontal devolution is between Union and States
Both terms refer only to grants to local bodies
accepted.x: Vertical devolution divides the divisible pool between the Union and States, while horizontal devolution distributes the States' share among the States.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two closely related fiscal terms by their direction of distribution.
accepted.sec: Vertical vs horizontal devolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who decides both vertical devolution and horizontal devolution in the framework described?
o: The GST Council alone
The Parliament through the Appropriation Act
The Finance Commission
The Reserve Bank of India
accepted.x: The Finance Commission determines the vertical division and the criteria for horizontal distribution of the States' share.
accepted.tq: Match the fiscal function with the constitutionally relevant recommending body.
accepted.sec: Vertical vs horizontal devolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the arrangement stated for the 15th and 16th Finance Commissions for 2026–31, what share of the divisible pool is assigned to the States under vertical devolution?
accepted.x: The stated share for States under vertical devolution is 41% under both the 15th and 16th Finance Commission framework for 2026–31.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the current stated percentage from the familiar earlier 32% and 42% figures.
accepted.sec: Vertical vs horizontal devolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a criterion for horizontal devolution?
o: Area
GST Council voting weight
Income distance
Population
accepted.x: Income distance, population, area, forest and other criteria are used for horizontal devolution. GST Council voting weight is unrelated to this distribution.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated institutional criterion in a fiscal-distribution list.
accepted.sec: Vertical vs horizontal devolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Vertical fiscal imbalance in India primarily reflects the fact that
o: The Union has the more buoyant taxes while States carry heavier spending duties
States have the more buoyant taxes and the Union has the heavier spending duties
Local bodies collect most buoyant taxes and undertake no major spending duties
Both Union and States have identical tax bases and spending responsibilities
accepted.x: Vertical fiscal imbalance arises because the Centre controls more buoyant taxes, while States bear major expenditure responsibilities such as health, education, agriculture and police.
accepted.tq: Match the direction of tax buoyancy with the direction of expenditure responsibility.
accepted.sec: Vertical vs horizontal devolution  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
With reference to the distribution of taxation powers, consider the following statements:
1. Stamp duties on bills of exchange and cheques are levied by the Union and collected and appropriated by the States.
2. Non-agricultural income tax is levied and collected by the Union and shared with the States.
3. Land revenue is a State tax collected and appropriated by the State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements correctly state the assigned or shared authority: stamp duties follow Article 268, income tax follows Article 270, and land revenue belongs to the State List.
accepted.tq: Combine different levy, collection and appropriation arrangements without reversing their authorities.
accepted.sec: Tax - levying, collecting and appropriating authority  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Corporation tax is shared with the States under the arrangement mentioned from which Constitutional Amendment?
o: 101st Amendment
80th Amendment
73rd Amendment
42nd Amendment
accepted.x: Corporation tax is levied and collected by the Union and has been shared with the States since the 80th Constitutional Amendment.
accepted.tq: Test the amendment number associated with a specific tax-sharing change.
accepted.sec: Tax - levying, collecting and appropriating authority  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about tax immunity between the Union and the States is correct?
o: Union property is exempt from State taxes and State property is exempt from Union taxes, subject to the stated exception
All commercial operations of States are constitutionally exempt from Union taxation
The Union may tax every item of State property without restriction
State-owned companies cannot be taxed by the Centre under any circumstances
accepted.x: Union property is exempt from State taxation and State property from Union taxation; however, the Centre can tax a State's commercial operations and State-owned companies.
accepted.tq: Use the general rule together with its specific exception rather than an absolute immunity claim.
accepted.sec: Tax - levying, collecting and appropriating authority  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Financial relations between the Union and the States are principally dealt with in which Part and range of Articles?
o: Part XII, Articles 268–293
Part X, Articles 245–263
Part XI, Articles 264–293
Part XIII, Articles 300–323
accepted.x: Part XII is titled Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits, and the financial-relations provisions stated here are Articles 268 to 293.
accepted.tq: Separate the Part number from the broader syllabus range and identify the exact constitutional framework.
accepted.sec: Financial relations framework - Part, Articles, emergencies, Consolidated Fund  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following receipts is credited to the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 266?
o: All Union revenues, loans raised and loan repayments received
Only grants received by local bodies
Only tax revenue collected by the Union
Only money held in trust for States
accepted.x: The Consolidated Fund of India receives all revenues of the Union, loans raised by it and loan repayments received by it.
accepted.tq: Test the complete constitutional list rather than the narrower phrase tax revenue.
accepted.sec: Financial relations framework - Part, Articles, emergencies, Consolidated Fund  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: No money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without an Appropriation Act under which provision?
o: Article 266(3)
Article 110(1)
Article 114(3)
Article 123
accepted.x: Article 114(3) requires an Appropriation Act before money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the withdrawal safeguard from nearby provisions relating to Money Bills and the Consolidated Fund.
accepted.sec: Financial relations framework - Part, Articles, emergencies, Consolidated Fund  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: During a National Emergency, the President may modify the distribution of revenues between the Union and the States under which Article?
o: Article 354
Article 352
Article 356
Article 360
accepted.x: Article 354 empowers the President to modify the distribution of revenues during a National Emergency.
accepted.tq: Use the Article-number trap among the constitutional emergency provisions.
accepted.sec: Financial relations framework - Part, Articles, emergencies, Consolidated Fund  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A modification of revenue distribution made under Article 354 continues until
o: the end of the financial year in which the Emergency ends
the National Emergency is revoked, irrespective of the financial year
the next session of Parliament only
the next Finance Commission report
accepted.x: The modification continues until the end of the financial year in which the National Emergency ends.
accepted.tq: Test the precise time limit rather than the more obvious end-of-emergency wording.
accepted.sec: Financial relations framework - Part, Articles, emergencies, Consolidated Fund  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a power of the Union during a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: To transfer all State taxes permanently to local bodies
To suspend the Constitution of every State
To direct States on financial propriety and require certain Money and Financial Bills to be reserved for the President
To abolish State Legislatures permanently
accepted.x: During a Financial Emergency, the Centre may issue directions to States regarding financial propriety and require Money and Financial Bills to be reserved for the President.
accepted.tq: Identify the actual financial direction powers while rejecting extreme constitutional consequences.
accepted.sec: Financial relations framework - Part, Articles, emergencies, Consolidated Fund  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A Bill affecting taxation in which States are interested can be introduced in Parliament only with
o: the prior recommendation of the President
the approval of every State Legislature
the recommendation of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
the prior consent of the GST Council alone
accepted.x: A Bill affecting taxation in which States are interested requires the President's prior recommendation before introduction.
accepted.tq: Ask who gives the required constitutional recommendation and avoid substituting a related authority.
accepted.sec: Financial relations framework - Part, Articles, emergencies, Consolidated Fund  [other exams, GROUP-II]
